title: an-entry-point-starts-the-loop-only-once
intention: superclaude — and any other entry point — starts the ground loop if and only if one is not already running, deciding by READING the liveness record, never by scanning for a process.
why: Akien named superclaude as ONE OF the entry points, so the guard cannot live in superclaude: it is a shared door and belongs with the thing it protects (Law 6). Otherwise every future entry point re-derives it, which is Law 1's defect.

falsifier.proves_red: Two entry points launched simultaneously produce TWO loops — the expensive direction, and the one the atomic claim exists for. Or: a loop alive but merely slow is declared dead inside the 5s window and a second is started beside it. Or: the guard reads liveness by scanning for a process instead of reading the record, which would work and would still be wrong — the record is the owned answer (Law 6).
